statement_record.book: Set is cocomplete — every small diagram of sets has a colimit; presented as a second proof of Proposition 3.6.1, obtained by applying Theorem 5.6.5(i) in Set^op to the monadic contravariant power-set functor P : Set^op -> Set.
statement_record.intree: Definition SetsCoend : Coend F (for every F : C^op ∏ C ⟶ Sets); Program Instance Sets_HasPushouts : HasPushouts Sets; Program Instance Sets_Cocartesian : @Cocartesian Sets; Program Instance Sets_Initial : @Initial Sets (Instance/Sets.v:265). Structure/Complete.v:119: Definition Cocomplete {C : Category} := ∀ (D : Category) (F : D ⟶ C), Colimit F.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the general statement is never made. `Cocomplete` is defined (Structure/Complete.v:119) but no category in the tree carries a `Cocomplete` (or `Complete`) inhabitant — `grep -rInE '@Cocomplete|@Complete' ` finds only hypothesis positions (Theory/Adamek/Corollaries.v:61, Construction/Comma/Limit.v, Adjunction/GAFT.v, Adjunction/SAFT.v). What IS proved for Sets is a shape-by-shape supply: initial object, binary coproducts, all pushouts, and all coends (the coend being the closest thing to a general colimit, since it is literally a quotient of a sum indexed by all objects of an arbitrary C, with the dinaturality congruence). The book's own proof route is unavailable in-tree: there is no power-set monad, no monadicity witness for it, and no Theorem 5.6.5.

gap: No `Cocomplete Sets` inhabitant, and no route to one: Sets has no coequalizer instance (`HasCoequalizers Sets` does not exist anywhere; grep 'HasCoequalizers' finds only the class at Structure/Coequalizer.v:68 and the reflexive-weakening instance) and no indexed/small-coproduct construction (`iprod` in Structure/Limit/Product.v is the LIMIT of a discrete diagram; there is no dual `icoprod`). Concretely proved colimit shapes in Sets: empty (Sets_Initial), binary coproduct, pushout, coend. Missing: general `Colimit F` for an arbitrary diagram F : D ⟶ Sets, hence the corollary itself; also missing is the book's proof apparatus (power-set monad, its monadicity, Theorem 5.6.5).
